reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Jaw claudication over age 50 means giant cell arteritis; treat before biopsy
Polyarteritis spares glomeruli and lungs and is ANCA negative
Kawasaki coronary aneurysms are prevented by timely immunoglobulin
Kaposi sarcoma is HHV8 driven in immunosuppression
reference.pathophysiology: Immune attack (ANCA neutrophil activation, immune complexes, granulomatous T cell injury) necroses vessel walls whose healing stenoses or weakens them into aneurysms, ischaemically injuring kidney, nerve, gut, skin or eye in size specific maps. Endothelial tumours instead proliferate vessel channels from benign malformations to angiosarcoma under viral (HHV8) or mutagenic drivers.
additionalDifferentials: Large versus medium versus small vessel patterns
Polyarteritis versus ANCA renal disease by glomerular involvement
Kaposi sarcoma versus bacillary angiomatosis in AIDS
additionalInvestigations: Temporal artery biopsy length adequate, after starting steroids
ANCA PR3 MPO with urinalysis and renal biopsy
Angiography for visceral microaneurysms in polyarteritis
